commenti.body: Martin Scorsese wanted to make this film perfect because it was supposed to be his last film. He decided to step away from film career after Ronald Reagan got shot by a man who wanted to impress Jodie Foster and his inspiration was Scorsese's classic crime drama Taxi Driver. This pushed Marty into a life of depression and substance abuse. So, when Scorsese decided to make this film at the request of his friend Robert De Niro, he wanted it to be a perfect one. There is no surprise if someone finds this film as his best work.

While it's true that Scorsese intended for Raging Bull to be his final film, the Reagan assassination happened a year after the release of Raging Bull. 

If I recall, Scorsese said that Raging Bull would be his last film, as he believed that no studio would want to work with him after that.
I've never heard the thing about Scorsese saying Raging Bull was his last film, why did he say that?

I disagree.

I don't think Raging Bull ever redeems Jake, not in the eyes of the audience, nor in his own eyes as a character in the movie or a real person. Raging Bull does humanise Jake, masterfully so, but this is not the same redeeming him. 

The audience is able to empathise with his plight, but that doesn't mean they understand or forgive his abhorrent behaviour towards his family.

As for Jake himself, while the movie shows that he eventually understands how fucked up he is and the mistakes he made, at no point does it show that he feels that he is redeemed for these mistakes

I agree but there is no specific evidence in the film that says this but it is all in the acting. There is a progression of scenes at the end of the film that illustrate this beautifully. It starts when Jake beats the wall in the prison cell, another act of repentance and self punishment. After this Jake seems to have lost his "Mojo". He is meek in his comedy club performance in a way we haven't seen before. Then he sees his brother and begs for his brother's forgiveness. He could not do this earlier in the film when he calls him but then hangs up.  In the final "Coulda been a contender" scene, Jake seems almost like a new person. He seems to have his pride back but also a little more dignity and calm. I know this doesn't prove anything but the acting is so powerful and it least to me says a hell of a lot.
